title: Efficient Interactive LLM Serving with Proxy Model-based Sequence Length Prediction
venue: arXiv preprint (v2 Nov 2024; AIOps'24 workshop version)
technique: speculative shortest-job-first (SSJF) scheduler using a fine-tuned BERT-base proxy model (regression, L1 loss) to predict output length; no change to batching/memory management

optimized_metrics.evidence: their interactive nature mandates low job completion times (JCT) and higher throughput for inference requests
their interactive nature mandates low job completion times (JCT) and higher throughput for inference requests

headline_claim.text: SSJF reduces average job completion times by 30.5-39.6% and increases throughput by 2.2-3.6x compared to FCFS schedulers, across no batching, dynamic batching, and continuous batching settings.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 4, 5 (average JCT vs rate and burstiness)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: (not defined) 'long job completion times (JCT)' attributed to 'high waiting times'
metric_definitions.notes: JCT used as end-to-end request latency incl. queueing (waiting time causes long JCT); never formally defined; average only (no tail)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: (not defined) 'the serving throughput' reported as relative improvement vs FCFS
metric_definitions.notes: units not stated; requests-based presumably; reported as multiples at varying request rate/burstiness

load_regime: Poisson-like arrival rate sweep and burstiness sweep using Microsoft Azure function traces for arrival times; LMSYS-Chat-1M prompts; batching: none / dynamic / continuous (max batch 4)
tradeoff_acknowledged: no starvation handling or preemption in SSJF (aging mentioned as option); gains shrink as batch size increases; pairwise predictor rejected for O(log N) cost
models: OPT-1.3b/2.7b, GPT2-large/xl, CodeGen-350m/2b, Bloom-1b1/3b, Switch-base-16/32 (small models)
workloads: LMSYS-Chat-1M; arrival times from Azure function traces
extractor_notes: JCT and throughput used without formal definition. Only mean JCT is reported (no percentiles). Small models on V100; continuous batching max batch size 4, so generalisation to modern serving is limited. Compared against FCFS and oracle SJF (oracle reduces JCT by 43-58%).
load_class_quote: Fig 4 and Fig 5 show the average LLM serving JCT with varying request arrival rates and burstiness (§4); arrival times from Azure function traces
